title: URL Filtering rule order and first match
aliases: why does rule A beat rule B

prose.text: URL Filtering is a first-match policy. {{ascending-order}} {{first-match}}

prose.label: Category first.
prose.text: Which category a URL is in is decided before any rule is walked: [[zia.url-categories.membership:resolved-before-rules]].

prose.label: Rules that never run.
prose.text: If Cloud App Control explicitly allows the transaction, URL Filtering does not run unless cascading is enabled ([[zia.cloud-app-control.precedence]]). On inspected HTTPS, URL Filtering runs twice, once on the domain and once on the full URL ([[zia.ssl-inspection.pipeline]]).

checks.do: Which category the URL belongs to, since it is resolved before any rule is walked.
Whether a higher rule fails to fire only because the URL resolved to a different category.
Whether a disabled rule is the reason a higher rule appears not to fire.
Whether an admin rank limits the positions a rule can take in the order.

ascending-order.statement: URL Filtering rules evaluate in ascending `order` (Rule 1 before Rule 2).

quotes: Policy rules are evaluated in ascending numerical order (Rule 1 before Rule 2, and so on)

first-match.statement: Evaluation stops at the first rule whose criteria all match; later rules are not consulted.

quotes: The evaluation of the policy rules stops at the first match.

disabled-holds-slot.statement: A disabled rule is skipped but keeps its position in the order.

quotes: A disabled rule is not actively enforced but does not lose its place in the rule order. The service skips it and moves to the next rule.

admin-rank-precedes.statement: With Admin Rank enabled, a rule's admin rank (0 is highest, 7 lowest) constrains the order values it can take: a higher-ranked rule always precedes a lower-ranked one, and an admin cannot pick a rank above their own.

quotes: Admin Rank: Enter a value from 0 to 7 (0 is the highest rank).
You cannot select a rank that is higher than your own.
so that a rule with a higher admin rank always precedes a rule with a lower admin rank.

admin-rank-order-collision.title: Whether two rules at different admin ranks can share an order value
admin-rank-order-collision.resolution: The console constrains the order values each admin rank can take so that a higher-ranked rule always precedes a lower-ranked one (claim admin-rank-precedes); with Admin Rank off, order is a flat sequence. No source describes two ranks sharing a value.
